questions.q: What is the primary physical setting of the poem "olar vk;k" and which two sensory details does the poet use to establish it in the first stanza?
questions.a: The primary setting is an agricultural field during daytime. The poet uses the visual detail "cM+s&cM+s fi;jk, iÙks" (large clods of earth, the sun) and the tactile detail "f[kyh gqbZ gok vkbZ" (scorching hot wind) to establish the harsh, sun-baked field. A wrong answer that says "village" or "home" shows the student cannot distinguish the specific locus of action; missing the sensory details indicates they are not reading for imagery.

questions.q: Explain in your own words how the description of the farmer's routine ("veqd fnu veqd ckj enueghus dh gksosxh iapeh") contributes to the atmosphere of the poem.
questions.a: The repetition of "veqd fnu veqd ckj" (day after day, time after time) and the image of the farmer's unchanging routine ("iapeh" — habit) creates an atmosphere of relentless, cyclical toil. It suggests a life governed by nature's rhythms, not human choice, evoking both weariness and quiet endurance. A wrong answer that focuses only on "hard work" without mentioning the cyclical, timeless quality misses the atmospheric depth — the poem is not about a single hard day but a lifetime of such days.

questions.q: In the poem "rksM+ks", the refrain "rksM+ks rksM+ks rksM+ks" appears at the start and end. Apply the concept of atmosphere to explain how this repetition shapes the mood differently in the two positions.
questions.a: At the start, the refrain acts as a rhythmic call to labor, setting an atmosphere of urgent, collective energy — the farmer urging himself and his tools into motion. At the end, after the stanza describing the heart's burden ("eu dh [kht"), the same refrain becomes a weary chant of persistence, shifting the atmosphere from outward action to inner resolve. A student who says "it shows the farmer works hard" in both cases fails to analyze the shift from external summons to internal compulsion.

questions.q: Compare the atmosphere created by the natural imagery in "olar vk;k" (e.g., "jax&jl&xaèk ls yns&i¡Qns nwj osQ fons'k") with the atmosphere created by the tool imagery in "rksM+ks" (e.g., "p^kusa] Ålj vkSj catj"). What does the contrast reveal about the farmer's relationship with his environment?
questions.a: The natural imagery in "olar vk;k" is vast, colorful, and indifferent ("jax&jl&xaèk" — multicolored, "yns&i¡Qns" — endless sky), creating an atmosphere of nature's overwhelming beauty and indifference. The tool imagery in "rksM+ks" is blunt, repetitive, and human-made ("p^kusa] Ålj vkSj catj" — axe, plough, spade), creating an atmosphere of deliberate, stubborn intervention. The contrast reveals the farmer as a small but determined agent imposing human will on a majestic, uncaring nature. A wrong answer that merely lists images without contrasting their emotional effect misses the analytical step.

questions.q: Evaluate the critic's statement: "The atmosphere of these poems is one of hopeless drudgery." Defend or refute using at least two textual evidences from either poem.
questions.a: The statement is partially true but incomplete. Evidence for drudgery: "ngj&ngj ngosaQxs dgha <kd osQ taxy" (deep, deep furrows, the back's strain) and "eu dh [kht" (burden of the heart). Evidence against hopelessness: the final refrain "xksM+ks xksM+ks xksM+ks" (break, break, break) implies breaking through, not giving up; and "fe^h esa jl gksxk gh tc og ikslsxh cht dks" (the crop will burn only when it ripens) shows faith in fruition. The atmosphere is better described as "stoic endurance with underlying hope." A student who agrees wholly ignores the poem's affirmative closure; one who denies drudgery ignores the physical toll.

questions.q: Write a four-line stanza in Hindi that creates an atmosphere of quiet resilience in a rural setting, using at least two sensory images and one tool reference. Do not copy lines from the textbook.
questions.a: A strong answer might be: "साँझ ढले खेत में हल की धार चमके, / थके कंधों पर चाँदनी का भार सजे। / मिट्टी की गंध लिए साँसें धीमी चलें, / कल फिर उगेगा बीज, यही विश्वास जगे।" It uses visual (moonlight on plough), olfactory (earth smell), and tool (plough) imagery to build quiet resilience. A poor answer uses generic city images or lacks sensory specificity, showing the student cannot transfer the concept to new creation.
